- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for early horizon (1–7 days) and 20–40% for mid/late horizon (8–30 days).  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects with exaggerated downward swings; cap downward corrections at 50% of peak deviation.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price history shows mean reversion, model tends to overpredict continuation; apply 10–20% downward bias to forecast if recent 5-day average is > 2.5.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early days (1–5) when sentiment is volatile; apply 10–25% downward adjustment to first 5 days if sentiment swings >0.5.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating high/low (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misreads trend direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3 days to anchor forecast if sentiment volatility >0.4.  
- If true outcome shows early sharp drop (first 3 days < 0.5), model often fails to recognize it; apply 20–30% upward bias to first 3 days if sentiment is low and price drops >1.5x recent mean.
